display.purpose: Stat block names, section headers inside notes, the app brand mark.

body.purpose: Chapter notes and statblock prose, 65–75ch measure.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked meta text — rail headers, callout titles, mono-hint fields. Substitutes for a UI/mono face.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: Stat-block and party-sheet modals over a blurred ink scrim.

shadows.name: fab
shadows.purpose: The floating 'Start Combat' button — the one persistent floating element on screen.

motion.name: hover-standard
motion.purpose: Named state transitions for buttons and rows; layout properties never animate.

motion.name: pulse-live
motion.purpose: Gold box-shadow ring on the combat FAB's dot, signalling the one live action.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Ink at rest, gold on hover — the system's core discipline: importance is ink, color is reserved for the moment of interaction.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 7px 12px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.01em; font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; transition: background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), transform 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary { background: #141414; color: #faf8f4; border-color: #141414; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.49 0.15 78); border-color: oklch(0.49 0.15 78); color: #ffffff; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.55 0.15 78); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Bordered, quiet default action button; the everyday button of the system.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #ffffff; color: #141414; border: 1px solid #e2ddd2; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: #5e5a54; background: #f3f0ea; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Hairline-bordered field; focus ring shifts to Antique Gold, the same accent used for button hover.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 7px 10px; border: 1px solid #e2ddd2; border-radius: 6px; background: #ffffff; font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; font-size: 13px; color: #141414; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #706b63; } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: oklch(0.55 0.15 78); outline: 2px solid oklch(0.55 0.15 78); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Mention Chip
components.description: Inline reference chip (creature/encounter link) — pill shape, gold-weak fill, uppercase gold prefix label.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 6px; border: 1px solid #e6e1d6; border-radius: 999px; background: oklch(0.95 0.045 78); padding: 1px 8px 2px; font-size: 12.5px; color: #141414; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: oklch(0.55 0.15 78); } .ds-chip-prefix { font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: oklch(0.55 0.15 78); font-size: 10px; }

components.name: Stat Block Popover
components.description: Sharp-cornered modal card — the one place the system breaks from the 6px radius, reading as a printed page lifted off the table.
components.css: .ds-popover { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e6e1d6; padding: 20px 24px; box-shadow: 0 24px 64px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); border-radius: 0; max-width: 420px; } .ds-popover-title { font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.1; letter-spacing: -0.01em; margin: 0 0 4px; color: #141414; } .ds-popover-meta { font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; font-style: italic; font-size: 13px; color: #6b6b6b; margin: 0; }

components.name: HP Bar
components.description: Party rail's signature component — health state uses ok/warn/danger, deliberately kept out of gold's hue family so it never reads as 'selected' or 'important'.
components.css: .ds-hp-bar { height: 6px; background: #e6e1d6; border-radius: 2px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-hp-fill { height: 100%; background: oklch(0.55 0.11 150); transition: width 180ms ease; }

narrative.overview:
Wish is a leather campaign ledger, not a game HUD. The DM Screen — the primary surface every other tool inherits from — is built on near-white paper, true-black ink, hairline rules, and a single serif voice carried through headings, body copy, and labels alike. Gold appears the way gold foil appears on a real ledger: rarely, on the spine and the important marks, never as a wash across the page. Buttons rest in ink and only turn gold on hover or focus; a small gold dot pulses on the one action that matters most (starting combat); selection and emphasis borrow gold sparingly. Everything else is disciplined: paper, ink, hairlines.

This system explicitly rejects the aesthetics of a generic SaaS dashboard (card grids, blue gradients, corporate chrome), a bright mobile-game fantasy UI (saturated gem-tone buttons, glossy icons), gritty grimdark (excess darkness, blood-and-grit heaviness), and any cartoonish or kids'-app treatment. It is calm, legible under table lighting, and built to disappear behind the words and numbers it's showing — because the DM Screen has to survive live play without slowing anyone down.

One correction this pass makes explicit: the accent that was actually implemented across every page was a muted terracotta/salmon (oklch(0.45 0.14 25)), while the project's own stylesheet comment already called the system "amber." That terracotta has been reassigned to the danger semantic role, where its warmth reads as alert rather than identity, and antique gold now carries the single primary accent everywhere.
keyCharacteristics: One serif family (Source Serif 4) does every job — display, body, and label — so hierarchy comes from weight, size, and letter-spacing, never a second typeface.
Gold is rare by design: hover states, the combat FAB's pulse, selection outlines, mention chips, and small semantic marks — never a resting button fill or a background wash.
Flat by default; shadows exist only for things that genuinely float (popovers, the floating action button).
Faction colors and semantic states are a separate palette from the brand accent — combat and bestiary readability never competes with gold for attention.
One light paper-and-ink theme is supported; dormant dark and parchment variants are intentionally excluded.
The canonical surface is an 11-inch iPad Pro in landscape, where party, notes, and reference columns remain visible.

rules.name: The Reserved Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold is not a fill color. It appears on hover, focus, selection, and small marks (dots and chip prefixes) — never as the resting background of a button, card, or panel.

rules.name: The Complete Border Rule
rules.body: Callouts, cards, rows, and alerts never use a thick coloured border on one side. Use a complete 1px hairline border, a small semantic dot, a full background change, or no container.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: --serif, --sans, and --mono all resolve to Source Serif 4. Do not introduce a second family for "UI" or "data" text — build hierarchy with weight, size, tracking, and case instead.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If it's sitting on the page, it's flat. Shadows appear only on the small set of elements that visually detach from the page flow (popovers, the FAB) — never on rows, cards, or rails.

dos: Do treat css/design-tokens.css as the shared token source of truth and css/dm-console.css as the component/layout reference.
Do use Antique Gold (oklch(0.55 0.15 78)) as the one primary accent, reserved for hover, focus, selection, and small marks.
Do keep the system flat by default; add shadow only to elements that float above the page.
Do build hierarchy with weight, size, tracking, and case within the single Source Serif 4 family.
Do keep faction and semantic colors visually distinct from the gold accent.
Do maintain the single light paper-and-ink theme and remove dormant variants.
Do preserve the three-column layout at the 11-inch iPad Pro landscape viewport.
Do use complete hairline borders and small semantic dots for callouts.
donts: Don't use the old terracotta/salmon (oklch(0.45 0.14 25), #932b2a) as a brand accent anywhere — it is now --danger only.
Don't fill a button, card, or panel with gold at rest.
Don't design toward a generic SaaS dashboard look.
Don't design toward a bright mobile-game fantasy UI.
Don't design toward cartoonish or kids'-app styling.
Don't introduce a second typeface for "UI" or "data" text.
Don't add rounded corners to popovers/modals.
Don't use thick coloured side borders on callouts, cards, rows, or alerts.
Don't add dark or parchment themes unless product requirements explicitly change.
